description: CHART 2 - Choropleth map with a year slider (advanced idiom: map). Shows the share of each country's farmland that is certified organic. Why a choropleth: the value belongs to an area (a country) and it is a standardised rate (organic land divided by all farmland), not a raw total, so big countries do not look dark just because they are big. Colour lightness shows low to high using ColorBrewer Greens in 6 classes. Projection: Equal Earth, which is equal-area, so country sizes are not distorted. The 'selected_year' parameter is bound to a range slider; every layer that filters on it redraws when the slider moves.

title.text: 15% of Australia's farmland is now certified organic, up from 3% in 2004
title.subtitle: Share of each country's farmland that is certified organic. Drag the slider to move through the years. Grey: no data.

layer.description: Layer 1: every country (except Antarctica, 'ATA') in warm grey. Countries with no data stay this grey because no coloured layer is drawn on top of them.

Layer 2: the coloured countries. It starts from the CSV (one row per country per year): filter to the year chosen on the slider, drop the Our World in Data aggregates (their codes are longer than 3 letters) and missing values, calculate share = organic / farmland x 100, turn the share into a class label ('band'), then 'lookup' joins each row to its country shape using the 3-letter code ADM0_A3 (ISO_A3 is -99 for France and Norway, so it can't be used). 'shape' with type geojson tells Vega-Lite to draw that joined shape.

transform.calculate: datum.share < 1 ? 'Under 1%' : datum.share < 2 ? '1–2%' : datum.share < 5 ? '2–5%' : datum.share < 10 ? '5–10%' : datum.share < 20 ? '10–20%' : '20% or more'

color.title: % of farmland that is certified organic

layer.description: Layer 3: Australia's outline in orange (no fill), so Australia stands out on every year of the slider.
Layer 4: a dynamic label under Australia that recalculates Australia's share for the selected year, placed at a fixed longitude and latitude in the Southern Ocean.
